items.title: Dalton Richards Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: The man is Mr. Cobb, I believe.

ctx.x: I can't think of Showboyd's name, but he was a good... I can't think of it, Alvin.

He's a good trombone player. He's a Dixieland trombone player. And, uh, we had Sidney Montague on drums, Howard Davis on trumpet, I mean on saxophone, alto sax and clarinet, Alvin Alcorn on trumpet, Alvin Alcorn was playing, would play banjo and guitar. See? When he played those Dixieland jobs, he used his banjo. And he really could sing, see? So, I mean, at that time I began liking it. One time we went to one of Celestan's jobs, he couldn't fulfill the engagement, so he asked Albert to take charge. We went to…
Oh, I see. Sure boy, is his name Worthy Thomas? Worthy Thomas. That's it, Worthy Thomas. I couldn't think of that. You sure know, he doesn't Worthy Thomas. That's it.
